threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still carry an umbrella on you at all times, thinking it might rain. Locals trust the clouds but never check the forecast.
Caught a lad singing to an empty seat on the 59 last night, thought he was gonna burst into tears. Brixton on a Friday, never a dull moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw an old man chatting with a pigeon outside Yummies, as if it were his long-lost friend. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you see art students setting up easels in the middle of a kebab shop, capturing the chaos and color of late-night life.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they know to avoid BART during major delays—everyone else is still checking their apps cluelessly while you’re already on a bus.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The guy in a chef's apron arguing with the bus driver about missed stops—only in the Tenderloin do these conversations feel like street theater.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss that Gràcia has its own unique street festivals, like Festa Major, where locals celebrate with handmade decorations and spontaneous concerts.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they still look up at the street signs, trying to decipher the Catalan names while missing the rhythms of the neighborhood.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’re still dodging the curbs at Broadway Market, thinking it's just a charming village, not realizing it's a tactical maze on Saturdays.
Caught a couple arguing on the N68 last night; she was furious about him nicking her chips. Classic late-night drama!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the old lady feeding the street cats while arguing with a pigeon. Only in Neukölln do the animals seem to have opinions.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop that's open till 5 AM, with a resident cat that greets you at the door like a bouncer.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local if they know which taco truck has the best al pastor on a rainy Tuesday. Tourists still think it's about the fancy restaurants.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, I saw a guy in a full suit giving a piggyback ride to his buddy, both laughing, as the bus swung into Valencia. Classic Mission.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can walk into any bar and get a table right away. The locals know to make reservations at places like La Pepita; it’s a game changer.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their bewildered look trying to navigate the Gràcia markets without any Catalan. They stand out like a sore thumb.
